entities.summary:
Jan van Virneburg served as Bishop of Utrecht from 1364 until his death in 1371. He had previously served as Prince and Bishop of Münster from 1363 to 1364. As Bishop of Utrecht, van Virneburg played a crucial role in the administration of the Archdiocese, overseeing the governance of the diocese and its extensive territories. His tenure was marked by significant events, including the Hundred Years' War and the rise of the Duchy of Burgundy. Van Virneburg's legacy extends beyond his administrative roles, as he was also a patron of the arts and a supporter of the University of Utrecht. His influence can still be seen in the modern-day governance of the Archdiocese of Utrecht and the surrounding region.

Van Virneburg's life and career demonstrate the complexities of medieval politics and the importance of religious leadership during this period. His experiences and decisions had far-reaching consequences, shaping the course of regional history and leaving a lasting impact on the region's development.

The life and legacy of Jan van Virneburg serve as a testament to the enduring significance of medieval religious leaders and their role in shaping the modern world.

Jan van Virneburg died on July 1, 1371, leaving behind a legacy that continues to inspire and inform our understanding of the medieval period.

The impact of Jan van Virneburg's life and career can be seen in the many institutions and cultural artifacts that continue to thrive today, a lasting testament to his influence and legacy.
